rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The isolated letter Qāf is not counted as a verse, unlike composite initials resembling a clause and matching verse endings.
rows.anchor: لم يعد ق آية ولا نظير له من نون وصاد لأنه مفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majīd means noble, exalted, great, and abundant in honor; its root also describes camels whose bellies grow large from plentiful grazing.
rows.anchor: المجيد الكريم المعظم والعظيم المكرم والمجد في كلامهم الشرف الواسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also means providing generous hospitality, as the cited verse and poem show.
rows.anchor: من البث والداء الدخيل المخامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Something ʿajīb or ʿajab is whatever has no known cause or explanation.
rows.anchor: والعجيب والعجب هو كل ما لا يعرف علته ولا سببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marīj means mixed and entangled, from sending one thing among others; the image also describes tangled branches and covenants mixed up and not kept.
rows.anchor: والمريج المختلط المتلبس وأصله إرسال الشيء مع غيره من المرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem uses marīj for something tangled by its many branches; the root also describes mixing up covenants and failing to fulfill them.
rows.anchor: أي قد التبس بكثرة شعبه ومرجت عهودهم وأمر خلطوها ولم يفوا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer is omitted and inferred as “you will surely be resurrected,” from the disbelievers' question about dying and becoming dust.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم في ق والقرآن المجيد محذوف يدل عليه إذا متنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the answer is “We know what the earth diminishes of them”; the lām is omitted because the preceding context supplies its meaning, as in 91:9.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الجواب قد علمنا ما تنقص الأرض منهم وحذفت اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The governing verb for “when we die” is implicit: the intended question is whether they will be resurrected after death.
rows.anchor: والعامل في أإذا متنا مضمر والتقدير أإذا متنا بعثنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes Qāf as one of God's names.
rows.anchor: اسم من أسماء الله تعالى عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك وعكرمة
rows.claim: Another report identifies Qāf as an emerald-green mountain encircling the earth, whose color gives the sky its greenness.
rows.anchor: اسم الجبل المحيط بالأرض من زمردة خضراء خضرة السماء منها عن الضحاك وعكرمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Qāf can mean that the matter is decreed or that what is to happen has been decreed, like the interpretation of Ḥā Mīm.
rows.anchor: معناه قضي الأمر أو قضي ما هو كائن كما قيل في حم حم الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by the Quran, noble with God, great in itself, and rich in benefit, asserts that people will be raised on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: أي الكريم على الله العظيم في نفسه الكثير الخير والنفع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative oath answer is that Muhammad is God's messenger: his people rejected him because they were astonished that a human from among them was sent, expecting only an angel.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تقديره والقرآن المجيد أن محمدا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers called Muhammad's message astonishing because they denied both a messenger from their own people and resurrection after death.
rows.anchor: فأنكروا رسالته وانكروا البعث بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deem return to life far beyond imagination and impossible, so they deny that it can occur.
rows.anchor: أي رد بعيد عن الأوهام وإعادة بعيدة عن الكون

words: قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what the earth consumes of their flesh and blood and decomposes of their bones, so restoring them poses no difficulty.
rows.anchor: ما تأكل الأرض من لحومهم ودمائهم وتبليه من عظامهم فلا يتعذر علينا ردهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guarded book is the Preserved Tablet, which retains everyone's number and names and omits nothing.
rows.anchor: أي لعدتهم وأسمائهم وهو اللوح المحفوظ لا يشذ عنه شيء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the book is protected from decay, or it is the record kept by the angels who write people's deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حفيظ أي محفوظ عن البلى والدروس وهو كتاب الحفظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth they rejected is identified either as the Quran or as the Messenger.
rows.anchor: والحق القرآن. وقيل: هو الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their affair is confused: they alternately called the Prophet mad, a sorcerer, or a poet, and the Quran sorcery, soothsaying, or fabrication, out of ignorance.
rows.anchor: فمرة قالوا مجنون وتارة قالوا ساحر وتارة قالوا شاعر فتحيروا في أمرهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says a people who abandon the truth have their affairs become confused.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن ما ترك قوم الحق إلا مرج أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the plants and other growths provisions for His servants; all provision is from God, by His direct act or by causing it, though people may idiomatically be said to provide for others.
rows.anchor: وكل رزق فهو من الله تعالى بأن يكون قد فعله أو فعل سببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water sent from heaven revives a barren, drought-stricken land that had grown nothing.
rows.anchor: أي بذلك الماء الذي أنزلناه من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God brings dead land to life with water, He will bring the dead out of their graves; power over either act entails power over the other.
rows.anchor: مثل ما أحيينا هذه الأرض الميتة بالماء نحيي الموتى يوم القيامة فيخرجون من قبورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People doubt resurrection because they regularly see rain revive land but have no customary experience of dead humans returning; reflection shows both acts are within God's power.
rows.anchor: رأوا العادة مستمرة في إحياء الموات من الأرض بنزول المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To dharā is to scatter dust by wind; adh­rā has the same sense.
rows.anchor: ذرت الريح التراب تذروه ذروا إذا طيرته وأذرته تذريه بمعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥubuk are rippling paths on the evening sky or smooth water stirred by wind; the word also describes curly hair and the beauty and evenness of crafted work.
rows.anchor: الحبك الطرائق التي تجري على الشيء كالطرائق التي ترى في المساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr's poem uses ḥubuk for the rippled pattern made on water by a fierce wind, supporting the sense of patterned paths.
rows.anchor: ريح خريق لضاحي مائه حبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharrāṣ means liar, while kharṣ is conjecture or estimation; its root suggests cutting out speech without a basis.
rows.anchor: والخراص الكذاب والخرص الظن والحدس وسمي الحزر حرصا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghamra is being covered by water or overwhelmed by debt; a generous lord is called ghamr because his gifts cover people.
rows.anchor: والغمرة من غمره الماء يغمره وغمره الدين إذا غطاه بكثرته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: For “the day they are tried over the Fire,” al-Zajjaj allows yawm to be an accusative adverb of the punishment's occurrence.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج يوم نصب على وجهين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj's second analysis gives yawm an accusative form but nominative syntactic force because it is annexed to a clause, as in cited poetry and 72:11 and 6:94.
rows.anchor: والآخر: أن يكون لفظة لفظ نصب ومعناه معنى رفع

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Asked by Ibn al-Kawwa while preaching, Ali identified the scatterers as winds, burden-bearers as clouds, smooth runners as ships, and distributors as angels; Ibn Abbas and Mujahid also transmit this interpretation.
rows.anchor: سأل أمير المؤمنين عليا ع وهو يخطب على المنبر فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scatterers are winds that disperse dust and plant debris.
rows.anchor: فالذاريات الرياح تذور التراب وهشيم النبت أي تفرقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden-bearing clouds carry heavy water from one land to another; wiqr is a load on the back or in the belly, while waqr can mean deafness.
rows.anchor: السحاب تحمل ثقلا من الماء من بلد إلى بلد فتصير موقرة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wiqr means the weight of a load carried on the back or in the belly; waqr means heaviness in the ear.
rows.anchor: والوقر بالكسر ثقل الحمل على ظهر أو في بطن والوقر ثقل الأذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The smooth runners are ships gliding easily over water wherever they are directed.
rows.anchor: السفن تجري ميسرة على الماء جريا سهلا إلى حيث سيرت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternative referents are clouds moving where God sends them or the seven planets: Sun, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي السحاب تجري يسرا إلى حيث سيرها الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distributors are angels who apportion affairs among creatures as commanded.
rows.anchor: الملائكة يقسمون الأمور بين الخلق على ما أمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by these things for their great benefits to people and the signs they contain of His oneness and artistry.
rows.anchor: أقسم الله تعالى بهذه الأشياء لكثرة ما فيها من المنافع للعباد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view construes the oath as being by the Lord of these things, since an oath may only be made by God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن التقدير فيها القسم برب هذه الأشياء لأنه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far and Abu Abd Allah say people may swear only by God, while God may swear by whichever creatures He wills.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله ع إنه لا يجوز لأحد أن يقسم إلا بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes dhū mirra as powerful and strong, citing Gabriel's lifting Lot's towns from the black water to heaven and his cry that killed Thamud.
rows.anchor: في خلقه عن الكلبي قال ومن قوته أنه اقتلع قرى قوم لوط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada interpret dhū mirra as sound health and fine constitution, free from defects.
rows.anchor: معناه ذو صحة وخلق حسن عن ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says mirra means movement through the air, going and returning, descending and ascending.
rows.anchor: ذو مرور في الهواء ذاهبا وجائيا ونازلا وصاعدا عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further formulation calls Gabriel strong in God's cause and physically sound, without illness or defect.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شديد القوى في ذات الله ذو مرة أي صحة في الجسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel settled into the form in which he was created after descending to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: جبرائيل على صورته التي خلق عليها بعد انحداره إلى محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He” refers again to Gabriel; the highest horizon is the eastern horizon, higher than the west on the earth's plain, not a location in the air.
rows.anchor: كناية عن جبرائيل ع أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel usually came in human form; after Muhammad asked to see his created form, he appeared from the east at Hira, filled the horizon, and Muhammad fainted; Gabriel then embraced him in human form.
rows.anchor: إن جبرائيل كان يأتي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صورة الآدميين

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say Gabriel came down to Muhammad from the highest horizon after becoming established there.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة ثم دنا جبرائيل ع بعد استوائه بالأفق الأعلى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats danna and tadalla as synonymous for nearness, with tadalla adding increased proximity; danna and qaruba can substitute for one another.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج معنى دنا وتدلى واحد لأن معنى دنا قرب وتدلى زاد في القرب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib interprets Gabriel's istiwā as rising to heaven after teaching Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ارتفع وعلا إلى السماء بعد أن علم محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم عن سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says Gabriel stood balanced in the air after descending quickly so the Prophet could see him.
rows.anchor: اعتدل واقفا في الهواء بعد أن كان ينزل بسرعة ليراه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra' interprets the phrase as Gabriel and Muhammad reaching the same height at the lowest heaven on the night of the Ascension.
rows.anchor: استوى جبرائيل ع ومحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأفق الأعلى يعني السماء الدنيا ليلة المعراج عن الفراء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة وعطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The distance was the length of two bows; qaws means the bow used for shooting, and the expression follows Arab idiom.
rows.anchor: القوس ما يرمى به عن مجاهد وعكرمة وعطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the conventional measure “two bows,” also expressed as qayb, qayd, or qād of a bow.
rows.anchor: يقال قاب قوسين وقيب قوس وقيد قوس وقاد قوس وهو اختيار الزجاج

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير وشقيق بن سلمة
rows.claim: Another interpretation measures the distance as two cubits; a report from Anas is described as prophetic, but its content is not included in this excerpt.
rows.anchor: وكان قدر ذراعين عن عبد الله بن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير وشقيق بن سلمة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the passage was revealed about al-Asi ibn Wa'il, who sometimes agreed with the Messenger in certain matters.
rows.anchor: العاص بن وائل السهمي وذلك أنه ربما كان يوافق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض الأمور عن السدي

rows.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
rows.claim: A report from Ata ibn Yasar concerns a man who set out to meet Muhammad seeking benefit, then a disbeliever offered to supply him and bear his sin in exchange for his provisions.
rows.anchor: واحمل عنك إثمك عن عطاء بن يسار

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi says it was revealed about Abu Jahl, who acknowledged Muhammad commanded noble morals but did not believe.
rows.anchor: أي لم يؤمن به عن محمد بن كعب القرظي

words: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership is an explanatory parenthesis between the opening statement and the promise to recompense wrongdoers and benefactors.
rows.anchor: وهذا اعتراض بين الآية الأولى وبين قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recompenses idolaters for their idolatry and those who worship Him alone with the Garden; on one analysis the lām marks consequence as His knowledge leads to their deserved reward.
rows.anchor: إذا كان أعلم بهم جازى كلا منهم بما يستحقه وذلك لام العاقبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām attaches to God's ownership: He created people to worship Him and charged them so He could recompense each for known deeds; it is a lām of purpose.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن اللام في ليجزي يتعلق بما في قوله ولله ما في السموات وما في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabāʾir are grave sins; fawāḥish is the plural of fāḥisha and denotes the ugliest and most heinous sins.
rows.anchor: جمع فاحشة وهي أقبح الذنوب وأفحشها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One definition makes a major sin any sin whose warning ends with Hell, and a fahisha any sin carrying a prescribed legal penalty.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل إن الكبيرة كل ذنب ختم بالنار والفاحشة كل ذنب فيه الحد

rows.speaker: قارئ
rows.claim: The singular reading kabīr al-ithm is used because the following noun is grammatically singular even though plurality is intended.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ كبير الإثم فلأنه يضاف إلى واحد في اللفظ وإن كان يراد به الكثرة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة والشعبي
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayra, and al-Sha'bi take lamam as minor sins such as looking or kissing and acts short of adultery.
rows.anchor: فقيل هو صغار الذنوب كالنظر والقبلة وما كان دون الزنا عن ابن مسعود وأبي هريرة والشعبي

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says lamam refers to sins committed in the pre-Islamic period and forgiven upon entering Islam, making the exception disconnected.
rows.anchor: ما ألموا به في الجاهلية من الإثم فهو معفو عنه في الإسلام عن زيد بن ثابت

rows.speaker: الحسن والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Suddi define lamam as committing a sin once, then repenting and not returning to it.
rows.anchor: أن يلم بالذنب مرة ثم يتوب ولا يعود عن الحسن والسدي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj's preferred view is that a person has lapsed into a sin but does not persist in it; God's vast forgiveness supports this reading, and Ibn Abbas applies it to the repentant.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار الزجاج لأنه قال اللمم هو أن يكون الإنسان قد ألم بالمعصية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's mercy encompasses all sins for the person who commits such a lapse and repents.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس لمن فعل ذلك وتاب ومعناه إن رحمته تسع جميع الذنوب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid says the amount of water from heaven was measured like the amount of water from earth.
rows.anchor: قدر ماء السماء مثل ما قدر ماء الأرض عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the water was sent according to a decree fixed for them in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه على أمر قدر عليهم في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was carried in a vessel assembled from planks fastened together; alwāḥ are its boards.
rows.anchor: سفينة ذات ألواح مركبة بعضها إلى بعض وألواحها خشباتها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd identify dusur as the nails fastening the vessel.
rows.anchor: مسامير شدت بها السفينة عن ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and others take dusur as the vessel's prow or chest, which cuts through the water.
rows.anchor: صدر السفينة يدسر بها الماء عن الحسن وجماعة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies dusur as the vessel's ribs.
rows.anchor: أ ضلاع السفينة عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says dusur are its two ends and bottom, while the planks are its sides.
rows.anchor: الدسر طرفاها وأصلها والألواح جانباها عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vessel sailed under God's protection and watch, as in the expression “God's eye is upon you.”
rows.anchor: أي بحفظنا وحراستنا وبمرأى منا ومنه قولهم عين الله عليك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God's eyes are the eyes of His angelic guardians assigned to the vessel.
rows.anchor: بأعين أولياؤنا ومن وكلناهم بها من الملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation takes the phrase as the water's springs that God caused to follow the vessel.
rows.anchor: تجري بأعين الماء التي أتبعناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saving Noah and drowning his deniers was recompense for the one whom they had rejected: Noah, whose prophethood and truth they denied and through whom they disbelieved God.
rows.anchor: ثوابا لمن كان قد كفر به وجحد أمره وهو نوح ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God left the deed He performed as a sign; alternatively, the preserved vessel, saved people, and destruction of the rest remain proof of divine unity and a lesson.
rows.anchor: أي تركنا هذه الفعلة التي فعلناها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the vessel remained until the earliest generations of this community saw it.
rows.anchor: وكانت السفينة باقية حتى رآها أوائل هذه الأمة عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether anyone will remember, recognize the truth, learn a lesson, and fear God.
rows.anchor: أي متذكر يعلم أن ذلك حق فيعتبر به ويخاف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada alternatively understands the phrase as asking whether anyone seeks knowledge and will be helped to it.
rows.anchor: فهل من طالب علم فيعان عليه عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is not informational but magnifies God's punishment and vengeance and the warning given to the people.
rows.anchor: هذا استفهام عن تلك الحالة ومعناه التعظيم لذلك العذاب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains nudhur as the plural of nadhīr, “warner.”
rows.anchor: النذر جمع نذير وإنما كرر سبحانه هذا القول في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is repeated throughout the sūra because, after detailing forms of warning and punishment, God recalls them individually.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر أنواع الإنذار والعذاب عقد التذكير بشيء منه على التفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Quran easy to memorize and recite; its clear expression, evident proofs, sound rulings, and true meanings make learning accessible and encourage people to gain knowledge.
rows.anchor: سهلناه للحفظ والقراءة حتى يقرأ كله ظاهرا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the Quran is the only revealed book that can be recited entirely from memory.
rows.anchor: إلا القرآن عن سعيد بن جبير والتيسير للشيء هو تسهيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making a path to knowledge easy is a strong reason to pursue it and gain a great share of learning.
rows.anchor: فمن سهل له طريق العلم فهو حقيق بأخذ الحظ الجزيل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance leads to knowledge: someone heedless of a thing or its proof cannot know it while heedless, but recalling the evidence and its paths opens knowledge in its proper way.
rows.anchor: لأن الساهي عن الشيء أو عن دليله لا يجوز أن يعلمه في حال سهوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question urges people to take heed, reflect, and consider the Quran.
rows.anchor: أي متعظ معتبر به ناظر فيه

rows.speaker: يعقوب عن رويس
rows.claim: Yaqub, through Ruways, reads sanuhzamu, “We shall defeat the gathered force”; the remaining readers read sayuhzamu, “the gathered force will be defeated.”
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب عن رويس سنهزم الجمع والباقون سيهزم الجمع

rows.speaker: أبو السماك
rows.claim: In a noncanonical reading, Abu al-Sammak reads anna with nominative kullu; the main reading has accusative kulla.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة أبي السماك أنا كل شيء بالرفع

rows.speaker: زهير والقرقني والأعمش
rows.claim: Zuhayr, al-Qarqani, and al-A'mash read nahr with two ḍammas.
rows.anchor: والأعمش ونهر بضمتين

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni prefers nominative kullu as a topic with a clause predicate, like “Zayd, I struck him”; innā changes the noun's case while the clause retains its structure.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني الرفع في قوله

rows.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid prefers accusative kullā, supplying an understood verb after innā from the preceding context.
rows.anchor: واختيار محمد بن يزيد النصب لأن تقديره إنا فعلنا كذا

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni rejects al-Mubarrid's argument: a nominal sentence's predicate is originally a noun, not a separate verb, and inna's predicate follows the same principle.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني وهذا ليس بشيء لأن الأصل في خبر المبتدأ أن يكون اسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuhur may be a plural of nahr on patterns like asad/asud, or a plural of nahar on patterns like saqf/suqf and rahan/ruhun.
rows.anchor: أن يكون جمع نهر كسقف وسقف ورهن ورهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan disbelievers are no better or stronger than Noah's, Ad's, or Thamud's peoples in worldly wealth, strength, numbers, or equipment; their predecessors' destruction warns them too.
rows.anchor: لستم أفضل من قوم نوح وعاد وثمود لا في القوة ولا في الثروة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no exemption in earlier scriptures promising that the punishment of past nations will spare them.
rows.anchor: ألكم براءة من العذاب في الكتب السالفة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the Meccans boast that they are united and will defeat their enemies.
rows.anchor: نحن جميع أمرنا ننتصر من أعدائنا عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muntasir is singular in form although it describes a collective plural, like rahṭ or jaysh.
rows.anchor: ووحد منتصر للفظ الجميع فإنه واحد في اللفظ وإن كان اسما للجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their unity cannot shield them from God's punishment, despite their claim that no one can attack or defeat them.
rows.anchor: فكذلك لا جمع لهم يمنع عنهم عذاب الله وينصرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathered force means the Meccan disbelievers, who will flee with their backs turned; their defeat at Badr fulfilled this prediction and was a prophetic miracle.
rows.anchor: فكان موافقة الخبر للمخبر من معجزاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ultimate appointment for their punishment is the Resurrection, whose harm is greater and more bitter than killing or captivity.
rows.anchor: أن ما يجري عليهم من القتل والأسر يوم بدر وغيره لا يخلصهم من عقاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā is more severe in harm; dahāʾ is a calamity with no means of removing it, and the afterlife's punishment is more bitter than worldly defeat.
rows.anchor: والدهاء عظم سبب الضرر مع شدة انزعاج النفس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation of greater bitterness is that punishment lasts longer, since the root of murr signifies passing through or continuing.
rows.anchor: الأمر الأشد في استمرار البلاء لأن أصل المر النفوذ

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the criminals have lost the path to salvation and Paradise and are in a blazing fire.
rows.anchor: أي في ذهاب عن وجه النجاة وطريق الجنة في نار مسعرة عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, dalāl means ruin and departure from truth, while suʿur means suffering and torment.
rows.anchor: في ضلال أي في هلاك وذهاب عن الحق وسعر أي عناء وعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day the angels drag the criminals face-first through the Fire and tell them to taste Saqar's heat and pain, like feeling a fever's touch.
rows.anchor: في يوم يجرهم الملائكة فيه على وجوههم في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is Hell; alternatively it is one of Hell's gates. The word derives from scorching and is indeclinable because it is feminine and definite.
rows.anchor: وسقر جهنم. وقيل: هي باب من أبوابها وأصل السقر التلويح

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says God creates each thing according to a measure required by wisdom, never aimlessly; punishment is proportioned to deserts and all things are measured.
rows.anchor: خلقنا كل شيء خلقناه مقدرا بمقدار توجبه الحكمة لم نخلقه جزافا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says each thing has a proper measured function: the tongue speaks, hand grasps, foot walks, eye sees, ear hears, and stomach digests food.
rows.anchor: فخلقنا اللسان للكلام واليد للبطش والرجل للمشي والعين للنظر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets qadar as fitting forms paired appropriately, such as woman and man, she-ass and donkey, and men's and women's clothing.
rows.anchor: جعلنا لكل شيء شكلا يوافقه ويصلح له كالمرأة للرجل والأتان للحمار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes qadar as a fixed measure and decree recorded in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خلقنا كل شيء بقدر مقدر وقضاء محتوم في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Kalbi compare the swift command bringing the Hour to an eye's blink: God restores all creation just as quickly.
rows.anchor: وما أمرنا بمجيء الساعة في السرعة إلا كطرف البصر عن ابن عباس والكلبي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says creating anything requires only one command, “Be,” with no second command, and happens without delay.
rows.anchor: وإنما نقول له كن فيكون كلمح البصر في سرعته من غير إبطاء ولا تأخير عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God destroyed earlier peoples resembling the addressees in disbelief; they are called their peers because they disbelieved and denied the prophets.
rows.anchor: أشباهكم ونظائركم في الكفر من الأمم الماضية عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning asks whether anyone will reflect and desist from the disbelievers' past conduct, lest the same destruction befall them.
rows.anchor: لما يوجبه هذا الوعظ من الانزجار عن مثل ما سلف من أعمال الكفار

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says every deed is in the books kept by the recording angels, showing that no one is overlooked.
rows.anchor: في الكتب التي كتبها الحفظة وهذه إشارة إلى أنهم غير مغفول عنهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, all deeds are written in the Preserved Tablet, a sign that future events are known in detail before they occur.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه أن جميع ذلك مكتوب عليهم في الكتاب المحفوظ

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says ships with raised sails are manshaʾāt; those whose sails are not raised do not have this description. Qilāʿ is the plural of sail.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد ما رفع له القلاع فهو منشأ وما لم ترفع قلاعه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says the ships are likened to mountains on land.
rows.anchor: شبه السفن في البحر بالجبال في البر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: With shīn read kasra, the ships produce waves with their prows as they move, the waves appearing like mountains.
rows.anchor: المنشئات بكسر الشين وهي أن ينشئ الموج بصدرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's teaching people to build ships and His making water suitable for their passage are favors to His servants.
rows.anchor: بأن علمهم اتخاذ السفن ليركبوها وإن جعل الماء على صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every living creature on earth perishes and passes out of existence.
rows.anchor: كل من على الأرض من حيوان فهو هالك يفنون ويخرجون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is understood though not previously named, as in the Medinan expression “between its two lava tracts.”
rows.anchor: كنى عن الأرض وإن لم يجر لها ذكر كقول أهل المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The face of your Lord” means the Lord Himself, enduring and manifest through His proofs as a person's face makes him manifest.
rows.anchor: ويبقى ربك الظاهر بأدلته ظهور الإنسان بوجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majesty denotes greatness, deserving praise, and supreme beneficence, the source of every favor; God honors prophets and friends with His subtle favors.
rows.anchor: أي العظمة والكبرياء واستحقاق الحمد والمدح بإحسانه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God is worthy of reverence and must be declared transcendent from what does not befit His attributes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه أهل أن يعظم وينزه عما لا يليق بصفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic idiom uses “face of the opinion” or “face of the plan” for the opinion or plan itself; al-A'sha's poem uses face for the settled judgment.
rows.anchor: وتقول العرب هذا وجه الرأي وهذا وجه التدبير بمعنى أنه الرأي والتدبير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes “face” the means by which one draws near to God, supported by a poem pairing God's face with deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن المراد بالوجه ما يتقرب به إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is a favor because it equalizes creatures, leads to reward, warns that worldly life ends, and gives moral agency: immediate reward would compel action and erase its merit.
rows.anchor: النعمة فيه التسوية بين الخلق فيه وأيضا فإنه وصلة إلى الثواب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the inhabitants of the heavens and earth need God and ask Him for their needs.
rows.anchor: لا يستغني عنه أهل السموات والأرض فيسألونه حوائجهم عن قتادة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says earthly people ask for provision and forgiveness, and angels also ask these for them.
rows.anchor: يسأله أهل الأرض الرزق والمغفرة وتسأل الملائكة لهم أيضا الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's daily acts include giving life and death, health and sickness, rescue and destruction, deprivation and giving, and innumerable other affairs.
rows.anchor: إن شانه سبحانه إحياء قوم وإماتة آخرين وعافية قوم ومرض آخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening, unattributed poetic fragment gives an Arabic usage parallel for khayra; al-Zajjaj says khayrāt is originally khayirāt, reduced by lightening.
rows.anchor:
ولقد طعنت مجامع الربلات
ربلات هند خيرة الملكات

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says khayrāt is originally khayirāt, reduced by lightening.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج أصل خيرات خيرات فخفف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiām are tents made of cloth stretched on poles and pegs, used in open country.
rows.anchor: والخيام جمع خيمة وهي بيت من الثياب على الأعمدة والأوتاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafraf may mean the gardens of Paradise, by comparison with a plant becoming fresh and green.
rows.anchor: والرفوف رياض الجنة من قولهم رف النبات يرف أي صار غضا نضرا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternative meanings of rafraf are seats, cushions, or any broad piece of cloth in Arabic.
rows.anchor: الرفوف المجالس. وقيل: الوسائد. وقيل:

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil's poem uses rafraf for broad, fine patterned cloth covering sandals.
rows.anchor:
قال ابن مقبل:
وإنا لنزالون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abqari refers to choice rugs and pile carpets embroidered with patterns; it is a collective noun with singular abqariyya.
rows.anchor: والعبقري عتاق الزرابي والطنافس المخملة الموشمة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says every rug is abqari and anything exceptionally fine is attributed to ʿAbqar, a place known for weaving carpets.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: كل شيء من البسط عبقري وكل ما بولغ في وصفه بالجودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are two further gardens besides the two promised to those who fear standing before their Lord; their nearness to the palace lets the blessed move joyfully between gardens and avoids boredom.
rows.anchor: ومن دون الجنتين اللتين ذكرناهما لمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان أخريان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dūn here is a locative term for a place nearer to something by comparison with another thing farther away.
rows.anchor: ومعنى دون هنا مكان قريب من الشيء بالإضافة إلى غيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the two gardens are lower in merit than the first pair; a prophetic report describes two gardens with silver vessels and contents and two with gold vessels and contents.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن المعنى أنهما دون الجنتين الأوليين في الفضل فقد روي عن النبي
